analysis.title: GS - Stankard - Eq Positioning and Key Levels - 26 Oct 2026
key_insights: CTAs are forecast to sell about $23.5bn of global equities this week (roughly -1 standard deviation in size). Estimated CTA long exposure is about $50bn of global equities, of which $36bn (72%) is SPX.
Base case is CTA selling of about $11.5bn of SPX this week while short-term trend remains negative.
GS Prime Brokerage: global equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (-0.6 SDs 1-year). De-grossing continued to accelerate, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1.
Single Stocks were net sold for a 6th straight week, driven by long sales. Macro Products were net bought for the first time in 3 weeks, driven by long buys.
US Single Stocks saw the largest de-grossing activity since late July. US equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (4 of the last 5, -0.9 SDs 1-year).
Staples was the most net bought global sector in dollar terms. HFs bought the sector at the fastest pace in 10 weeks, driven by long buys and short covers.
Staples and Real Estate (defensives and bond proxies) were by far the most net bought US sectors. Real Estate net buying was the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs 1-year).

HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months, driven by short and long sales. Within Energy, selling in Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels outpaced modest buying in Energy Equipment & Services.

US Industrials was among the most net sold US sectors, with long and short sales at 2.5 to 1. HFs sold the sector for a 2nd straight week (7 of the last 8) at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs 1-year).

Hedge fund net leverage is very low. Overall book net leverage is 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year), and Fundamental L/S net leverage is 47.0% (1-year low). Gross leverage is 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year).

Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell -1.28% from 10/16 to 10/22 against MSCI World TR at -0.76%, driven by beta of -0.98% and alpha of -0.30% from short-side losses. Systematic L/S fell -1.26%, driven by alpha of -1.63%.

About 27% of the S&P 500 is currently in an open buyback window, rising to about 50% by the end of the week. GS expects buyback volumes to pick up into November, seasonally its second most active execution month.

Buyback execution mix: discretionary orders rose to 16% versus 84% in 10b5-1 plans, from 15% and 85% the prior week. Last week's desk flows were 0.7x both 2025 YTD and 2024 YTD ADTV, skewed toward Financials, Health Care and Consumer Discretionary.
CTA key SPX pivot levels are 7717 (short term), 7532 (medium term) and 7070 (long term).

sector_views.rationale: Most net bought global sector by HFs this week at the fastest pace in 10 weeks. This is a flow observation, not a GS rating.
Most net bought US sector in standard-deviation terms, the largest net buying in more than 5 years. This is a flow observation, not a GS rating.
HFs net sold the US sector for a 2nd straight week at the fastest pace in more than 6 months. This is a flow observation, not a GS rating.
HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months. This is a flow observation, not a GS rating.

earnings_insights: A substantial portion of the S&P 500 reports results this week. The share of the index in an open buyback window is expected to rise from about 27% to about 50% by the end of the week as reporting progresses.
risk_factors: CTA selling accelerates if the tape falls. The down-tape scenario implies $60.70B of selling over 1 week and $172.52B over 1 month.
Short-term trend remains negative, which drives the base-case CTA selling.
HF de-grossing is accelerating, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1.
Short-side losses drove the negative alpha for both Fundamental and Systematic L/S performance estimates.
vol_and_positioning: CTA flow forecasts over the next 1 week: flat tape, sellers of $23.61B ($15.01B out of the US). Up tape, buyers of $3.60B ($7.14B out of the US). Down tape, sellers of $60.70B ($31.23B out of the US).

CTA flow forecasts over the next 1 month: flat tape, sellers of $36.42B ($17.02B out of the US). Up tape, buyers of $114.38B ($31.98B into the US). Down tape, sellers of $172.52B ($75.34B out of the US).
A 1x standard-deviation market move is 1.62% over 1 week and 3.78% over 1 month.
Overall book L/S ratio fell -0.7% to 1.597 (3rd percentile 1-year). US Fundamental L/S ratio (MV) fell -0.7% to 1.503 (0th percentile five-year).
US L/S gross leverage rose 2.2 pts to 216.1% (64th percentile 1-year). US L/S net leverage fell 0.3 pts to 43.4% (0th percentile five-year).
Beta Adjusted Fundamental L/S Gross leverage fell 1.9 pts to 226.5% (25th percentile 1-year). Beta Adjusted Net leverage fell 3.5 pts to 60.4% (1-year low).
Staples gross/net allocations in the global Prime book are 4.6%/1.4%, in the 70th/57th percentiles versus the past year and the 23rd/13th percentiles versus the past five years.

Charts in Focus covers the US Panic Index, Risk Appetite Indicator, SPX vs. Singles Skew, Call Skew vs. Put Skew, S&P Futures Liquidity, Funding Spreads vs S&P 500 and S&P 500 Implied Correlation. The text gives no chart readings.
